request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: an explainable boosting machine (EBM), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `utilization`: revolving credit utilization: the share of the credit limit in use (0 to 1).
  Share of importance 24.4% (95% band 21.0% to 26.2%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.214: -0.746; 0.214 <= x < 0.602: 0; 0.602 <= x < 0.712: +0.7; x >= 0.712: +2.8 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +3.57, 95% band [+2.81, +4.15]).
- `n_delinquencies`: number of past delinquencies on the credit file (0 to 6).
  Share of importance 18.3% (95% band 13.7% to 20.8%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.5; >= 1: +0.4 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.99, 95% band [+0.68, +1.16]).
- `income`: annual income in US dollars.
  Share of importance 9.2% (95% band 6.3% to 14.2%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 68,500: +0.043; x >= 68,500: 0 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.62, 95% band [-1.24, -0.45]).
- `history_months`: length of the credit history in months.
  Share of importance 6.7% (95% band 1.8% to 9.2%); rank 3 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.41 (95% band [-0.73, -0.03]) from x = 23.5 (5th percentile) to x = 343 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `feature_b`: an application attribute (standardised).
  Share of importance 3.2% (95% band 0.6% to 6.0%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.15, 95% band [-0.57, +0.10]).
- `dti`: debt-to-income ratio (0 to 0.6).
  Share of importance 2.6% (95% band 0.8% to 7.7%); rank 4 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.19 (95% band [+0.01, +0.56]) from x = 0.0282 (5th percentile) to x = 0.572 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `n_inquiries`: number of recent credit inquiries.
  Share of importance 1.6% (95% band 0.0% to 3.6%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.08, 95% band [-0.33, +0.15]).
- `feature_a`: an application attribute (standardised).
  Share of importance 1.4% (95% band 0.3% to 4.6%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.03, 95% band [-0.12, +0.36]).
- `age`: age of the applicant in years.
  Share of importance 0.3% (95% band 0.2% to 4.2%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.02, 95% band [-0.36, +0.21]).

Interactions: the model has 5 pairs. The larger ones:
- `utilization & n_delinquencies`: share of importance 19.1% (95% band 13.9% to 19.6%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0986 to 0.751: +1.02 (95% band +0.30 to +1.85) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, +6.07 (95% band +4.97 to +6.95) when `n_delinquencies` = 2.
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 2: -0.73 (95% band -1.30 to -0.31) when `utilization` = 0.0986, +4.33 (95% band +3.08 to +5.03) when `utilization` = 0.751.
- `history_months & n_inquiries`: share of importance 4.5% (95% band 0.0% to 5.9%).
  Effect of `history_months` from 23.5 to 343: +0.13 (95% band -0.59 to +0.53) when `n_inquiries` = 0, -1.45 (95% band -2.00 to -0.06) when `n_inquiries` = 4.
  Effect of `n_inquiries` from 0 to 4: +0.67 (95% band -0.06 to +1.02) when `history_months` = 23.5, -0.91 (95% band -1.47 to +0.06) when `history_months` = 343.
- `utilization & history_months`: share of importance 3.2% (95% band 0.0% to 5.3%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0986 to 0.751: +3.28 (95% band +2.34 to +3.98) when `history_months` = 23.5, +4.27 (95% band +2.89 to +5.17) when `history_months` = 343.
  Effect of `history_months` from 23.5 to 343: -1.08 (95% band -1.92 to -0.04) when `utilization` = 0.0986, -0.09 (95% band -0.58 to +0.29) when `utilization` = 0.751.
- `feature_a & feature_b`: share of importance 3.1% (95% band 0.0% to 4.6%).
  Effect of `feature_a` from -1.64 to 1.67: -0.57 (95% band -1.06 to +0.30) when `feature_b` = -1.63, +0.06 (95% band -0.42 to +0.56) when `feature_b` = 1.62.
  Effect of `feature_b` from -1.63 to 1.62: -0.59 (95% band -1.29 to +0.10) when `feature_a` = -1.64, +0.04 (95% band -0.46 to +0.49) when `feature_a` = 1.67.
- `utilization & feature_b`: share of importance 2.3% (95% band 0.0% to 3.8%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0986 to 0.751: +3.49 (95% band +2.81 to +4.22) when `feature_b` = -1.63, +3.22 (95% band +2.62 to +4.18) when `feature_b` = 1.62.
  Effect of `feature_b` from -1.63 to 1.62: -0.35 (95% band -0.86 to +0.38) when `utilization` = 0.0986, -0.62 (95% band -0.92 to +0.08) when `utilization` = 0.751.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"Revolving credit utilization is the strongest driver of predicted default: applicants using 71% or more of their credit limit carry a large increase in default risk (about +2.8 on the log-odds scale), while those below 21% carry a modest reduction."},{"id":2,"text":"Past delinquencies are the second most important driver: having at least one delinquency raises predicted risk, and the effect is roughly +0.9 log-odds higher going from none to two or more on the typical range."},{"id":3,"text":"The two leading drivers interact strongly: a delinquency history makes high utilization far more dangerous, so the effect of utilization is about six times larger for applicants with two delinquencies than for those with none."},{"id":4,"text":"Income, length of credit history, and debt-to-income ratio have smaller effects: higher income and longer credit history are associated with lower predicted risk, and a higher debt-to-income ratio with somewhat higher risk, though these effects are modest and their bands are wide."},{"id":5,"text":"Several interactions involving credit history length, recent inquiries, and two standardised application attributes are real in the model but uncertain, since their confidence bands include zero, so the data do not settle how strong they are."},{"id":6,"text":"The remaining features (recent inquiries, the two standardised application attributes, and age) show no resolved effect on predictions at this sample size and should not be read as drivers of default."}]}
